overview: Two nearly opposite processes — one builds glucose using light energy, the other breaks glucose down to release energy.
genZNote: Photosynthesis: cooking glucose using sunlight. Respiration: eating that glucose to power everything else.

aspects.label: Overall Direction
aspects.valueA: Builds glucose from CO2 and water (anabolic), storing energy.
aspects.valueB: Breaks down glucose into CO2 and water (catabolic), releasing energy.

aspects.label: Energy Flow
aspects.valueA: Captures light energy and converts it into chemical energy.
aspects.valueB: Releases stored chemical energy as ATP.

aspects.label: Occurs In
aspects.valueA: Only in cells containing chloroplasts (plants, algae, some bacteria).
aspects.valueB: In virtually all living cells (plants and animals alike).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Plants perform both photosynthesis and respiration continuously — they're not mutually exclusive, since plant cells still need ATP around the clock.
overlay.memoryTrick: Photosynthesis makes food using light. Respiration burns food to make energy.
overlay.commonMisconception: Plants do not stop respiring during the day just because they're photosynthesising — both processes run simultaneously in green plant cells.
